For an owner in Mexico who wants **brand affiliation** but still needs to preserve **greater hotel individuality**, the brands most commonly considered are **soft-brand** or **collection-style** options rather than highly standardized chains.[6][8][20]

Commonly cited choices include:

- **Preferred Hotels & Resorts** — a collection model that lets independent hotels keep their own identity while affiliating with a larger brand.[20]
- **Design Hotels** — typically used for design-led, distinctive properties that want brand recognition without losing a strong local or independent character.[4]
- **Leading Hotels of the World** — another luxury collection model suited to properties that remain highly individual.[16]
- **Radisson Individuals** — explicitly positioned to preserve each hotel’s unique character and boutique personality while meeting Radisson standards.[6]
- **Grupo MX / Alianzas MX** — a Mexico-based platform that says it works with independent hotels that want to preserve their identity while gaining corporate support.[8]

In Mexico specifically, **Grupo Habita** is often referenced as the benchmark for this model because it emphasizes that each property is “a one off” and refuses copy-paste standardization.[1][7][9][15] If the owner wants a more Mexico-rooted but still branded route, **Camino Real / Quinta Real / Real Inn** or **Atelier de Hoteles** may also come up, though they are generally more brand-defined than true independence-preserving collections.[2][3][5]

If you want, I can narrow this to **luxury**, **upper-upscale**, or **midscale** options in Mexico and compare the best fit for preserving individuality.
